courses.title: Fundamentals of Counseling Theories
courses.tagline: The maps every counselor carries into the therapy room.
courses.description: A rigorous survey of the major systems of psychotherapy, from psychoanalytic and Adlerian foundations through person-centered, Gestalt, reality, and contemporary cognitive, behavioral, and integrative models, each examined for its view of the child and the adolescent.
outcomes: Explain the major schools of counseling theory
Compare key concepts across each theoretical system
Analyze how each theory treats child and adolescent care
Begin shaping your own integrative counseling framework
Apply theory to real young-client case vignettes
modules: Foundations and History of Counseling Theory
Building Your Personal Theory of Practice
courses.practicum: Theory-to-practice case seminars, live demonstration analyses, and guided reflective journals.
courses.assessment: Theory comparison matrix, recorded integrative case formulation, and a comprehensive examination.

courses.title: Child Development Theories
courses.tagline: From first steps to first identities.
courses.description: A developmental journey through infancy, early childhood, and middle childhood, integrating Piaget, Erikson, Vygotsky, and Bowlby with contemporary neuroscience, attachment research, and the cultural contexts that shape every growing child.
outcomes: Describe milestones across all domains of child development
Apply Piaget, Erikson, Vygotsky and Bowlby in practice
Interpret attachment patterns in clinical settings
Distinguish typical development from early warning signs
Use developmentally informed intake and assessment tools
modules: Early Childhood: Play, Language and Self
Middle Childhood: Cognition and Social Worlds
courses.practicum: Observation studies, developmental milestone charting, and attachment-pattern case laboratories.
courses.assessment: Milestone analysis portfolio, child observation report, and a developmental case study.

courses.title: Adolescent Development
courses.tagline: Understanding the storm, the struggle, and the strength of adolescence.
courses.description: An in-depth study of adolescent physical, cognitive, moral, and identity development, addressing risk and resilience, peer culture, digital life, family transitions, and faith formation, and preparing counselors to walk with adolescents through one of life's most intense passages.
outcomes: Map adolescent development across every major domain
Apply identity and moral development theories in counseling
Assess adolescent risk and protective factors
Engage adolescent clients with developmental empathy
Design developmentally appropriate counseling plans
modules: Puberty, Body Image and Physical Change
Peers, Culture and the Digital World
Risk, Resilience and Positive Youth Development
courses.practicum: Adolescent interview practice, risk-and-resilience mapping, and youth-culture case discussions.
courses.assessment: Adolescent profile case study, developmental interview recording, and module examinations.

courses.title: Ethics in Counseling
courses.description: A comprehensive study of professional ethics in counseling with children and adolescents: confidentiality and its limits, consent and assent, boundaries, mandated reporting, dual relationships, and culturally humble, faith-informed ethical decision-making.
outcomes: Master the major counseling ethics codes and standards
Apply structured ethical decision-making models
Navigate confidentiality and consent with minors
Recognize and respond to mandated reporting duties
Build safeguards against boundary violations
courses.practicum: Ethical dilemma simulation labs and structured case-consultation exercises.
courses.assessment: Ethics decision case portfolio and a comprehensive ethics examination.

courses.title: Counseling Techniques and Skills
courses.description: The flagship skills laboratory of the program: microskills training, the structure of the counseling session, empathy and advanced attending, working alliances with children, adolescents, and caregivers, and deliberate practice with feedback until skill becomes habit.
outcomes: Demonstrate core microskills with fluency
Structure counseling sessions from opening to closing
Build strong alliances with young clients and caregivers
Use self-awareness as a clinical instrument
Respond effectively to resistance and silence
modules: Building Alliance with Children and Adolescents
courses.practicum: Recorded microskills laboratories with structured faculty feedback and live supervision.
courses.assessment: Recorded skills demonstrations rated with standardized microskills rubrics.

courses.title: Group Counseling for Children and Adolescents
courses.description: The theory and practice of therapeutic groups with young people: group stages and dynamics, screening and composition, play-based and expressive formats, school-based groups, and leading groups for grief, social skills, anger, and anxiety.
outcomes: Design developmentally appropriate counseling groups
Facilitate every stage of the group process
Screen and compose groups for young clients
Manage group dynamics and difficult moments
Evaluate group counseling outcomes
modules: Foundations of Group Work with Young People
